hackathon.name: Pharmacy Supply Challenge
hackathon.problem_statement: Pharmacies struggle to know what medicine to reorder and when. Stock runs out on essential medicines while slow-moving items tie up capital, and decisions are made from memory instead of data.
hackathon.requirements:
- Ingest historical purchase and stock dataset
- Produce a demand forecast per medicine for a configurable future window
- Recommend reorder quantity and reorder date per medicine
- Surface low-stock risk before stockout happens
- Show a confidence or data-quality signal for each recommendation
- Provide an interface a pharmacist can use in a few seconds per item
hackathon.constraints:
- No paid third-party data services
- No patient data may be stored
- Data must not be entered manually
hackathon.expected_outcome: A working prototype in which a pharmacist can open a dashboard, see which medicines are at risk of stocking out, understand why, and either accept the suggested reorder or adjust it.
hackathon.evaluation_criteria:
- Forecast quality and whether the method is explained
- Honesty about uncertainty and data gaps
- Usability for a pharmacist under time pressure
- Engineering quality of the implementation

submission.project_description: MediStock analyses historical pharmacy sales and batch stock to forecast demand per medicine, recommend reorder quantity and date, and warn about medicines likely to stock out. A dashboard lets a pharmacist review and adjust each recommendation.
submission.key_features:
- Demand trend and forecast per medicine
- Reorder quantity and date recommendation
- Low-stock and stockout risk alerts
- Purchase order creation and status tracking
- Inventory and batch level views
submission.tech_stack: Python, FastAPI, scikit-learn, pandas, SQLite, vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript
